items.title: Live: Resident says roofs lost, trees felled as Cyclone Narelle tears into Far North Queensland
items.description: Tropical Cyclone Narelle is crossing the Far North Queensland coast. Follow live.

items.title: Mosque vows to keep doors open after Albanese and Burke confronted
items.description: An event to mark the end of Ramadan was disrupted by a protest against the prime minister and home affairs minister, who were visiting the mosque in Western Sydney.

items.title: Live: Albanese denies Australia out of step with allies after joint statement
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese denies Australia is out of step with its allies after several countries, including the UK, France and Germany, released a joint statement on the Strait of Hormuz. Follow live.

items.title: Why the gas giants have suddenly gone to ground over Iran
items.description: Are Australians about to endure a re-run of the economic pain brought on by the Ukraine war? Or something much worse?

items.title: While the US is busy in Iran, China is pushing on with its geopolitical agenda
items.description: Donald Trump has postponed a meeting with Xi Jinping because he is busy with Iran and the Middle East — and that's good news for China.

items.title: One Nation candidate wanted in UK on sexual touching charge
items.description: South Australian One Nation candidate Aoi Baxter has a warrant for his arrest in the UK after he failed to show up to court to face a charge of sexually touching a woman without consent.

items.title: Video shows reporter narrowly avoiding Israeli strike in southern Lebanon
items.description: An English-language Russian state broadcaster has accused Israel of deliberately attacking its news crew in southern Lebanon. The IDF says it will investigate.

items.title: We might have just found where Australia's red line is with Donald Trump
items.description: The war in the Middle East is heaping pressure on Australia's relationship with the US and we could be about to see if that comes with consequences.

items.title: Trump jokes about Pearl Harbor in front of visibly uncomfortable Japanese PM
items.description: When he was asked why the US did not notify allies like Japan ahead of the strikes on Iran, Donald Trump made a quip drawing a parallel with the Japanese air raid in 1941.

items.title: Live: Major bank says oil price could soar to $US150
items.description: The CBA says there is a "strong likelihood" of the oil price reaching $US120‑150 per barrel. Follow the day's events and insights as they happen with our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Banksy's anonymity has been shredded along with the mystery of his work
items.description: Does Banksy's success mean we are more entitled to demand he pull his mask off, show his face? Does it matter that he says his anonymity is core to his art?

items.title: 'Asking why honey is better than s***': Japan coach spins favouritism ahead of Matildas clash
items.description: Japan's coach says determining a favourite for the Women's Asian Cup final between his team and Australia is a matter for bees and flies.

items.title: Sydney man jailed for 28 years after murdering 3yo son
items.description: Nathan Vikatos has been jailed for more than 28 years for what a judge described as the tragic, horrific and untimely death of his three-year-old son, Alexi, in May 2023.

items.title: Teen happiness falls in western countries as social media hours rise
items.description: The 2026 World Happiness Report links heavy social media use to a sharp decline in young people's wellbeing, with teenage girls in English-speaking countries and Western Europe among the most affected.

items.title: 'Look like cereal boxes': Uniforms are a factor in girls dropping out of sport
items.description: Studies in Australia and overseas show a big percentage of girls drop out of sport when they become teenagers. One of the contributing factors is the clothes they have to wear.

items.title: How to choose sheets and bed linen that last as long as possible
items.description: Shopping for sheets can be overwhelming and expensive. This is what textile experts say to look out for.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: History-making Oscars moments, a royal visit and fans storm the NRL field
items.description: It's been a big week in the news. Did you catch these stories?

items.title: With new James Blake and a sun-drenched crime drama we've got your weekend covered
items.description: This weekend go down the rabbit hole with a podcast about a Canadian cult or discover James Blake's latest sonic salve.

items.title: Former childcare worker jailed for indecent treatment of child
items.description: A former childcare worker from Fiji is sentenced to jail for the indecent treatment of a child at a daycare centre in Queensland, and will be deported afterwards.

items.title: Queensland police raid Christian organisation over pro-Palestine banner
items.description: Officers raid Dorothy Day House in Greenslopes over a banner with the slogan "From the River to the Sea", which is now a prohibited expression in Queensland.

items.title: Concerns lack of flood mitigation leaving Alice Springs dangerously exposed
items.description: A shock flash flooding event in Alice Springs last month saw more than 100 millimetres of rain fall on the catchment in a matter of hours. The deluge has reignited calls for urgent action on flood mitigation in the outback town, as insurance companies calculate the risk with eye-watering premiums.

items.title: How gas shortages are hitting hard in Asia
items.description: The Middle East war triggers everything from fuel rationing in Sri Lanka to a helium supply crisis for Asia's crucial semiconductor industries.

items.title: Is Australia actually running out of fuel?
items.description: We've all seen the headlines — Australia only has 30 days of fuel in reserve. But is that really the case? Reporting by Luke Radford for ABC News Loop.

items.title: 'The ABC got lucky': How the VFA became must-watch TV for footy fans
items.description: As Aussie Rules was forced to reckon with a national competition, four men helped make the VFA must-watch TV on the ABC for Victorian footy fans.

items.title: Poverty increased after 2022 Victorian floods, report finds
items.description: Poverty and unemployment rose after Victoria's 2022 floods, with those in inundated areas experiencing lower disposable income than those who weren't affected, according to a new report.
